resources.string: Shows lyrics the player itself publishes.
The lyric overlay is stored twice, once per theme. You are editing the NIGHT set; switching to day loads the other one.
The lyric overlay is stored twice, once per theme. You are editing the DAY set; switching to night loads the other one.
Affects these settings pages only. The lyric overlay keeps its own colours under “Colours”.

After boot, start AnyLyric in the background: ask the system to rebind the notification listener, and show the overlay right away (“waiting for playback”) so the boot result is visible. Some car units delay or drop the binding, which shows up as “no lyrics until the app is opened once”. Off by default.

Every 15 minutes, check a heartbeat and ask the system to rebind if the listener silently died. Some car ROMs kill background services without notifying the app. Off by default; no foreground service and no wake locks.
This head unit does not allow apps to ask

The system answers with “the multimedia system does not support this operation” because the manufacturer blocked the request page. The app is not broken.
Try the manual path: Settings → Apps → AnyLyric → Battery / Power management → Unrestricted.
If that entry does not exist, it is fine: turn on “Start on boot” above and “Periodic rebind” below, which also get the service back after the system kills it.
Ask the system to skip battery optimization for AnyLyric. The switch reflects the real system state; turning it off is done on the system page.

Music usually goes through one player in a car. Automatic picks whichever session is playing, and navigation prompts or leftover sessions can steal it; pinning reads only that one and shows nothing while it has no session.
Only this app is read. While it has no media session, no lyrics are shown.
Pick from whichever session is playing
No active media session right now. Start playing something, then come back.
Pinned “%1$s” has no media session right now — switch players, or set Player channel back to Automatic

When one of the selected apps comes to the foreground, both the lyrics and the collapse handle step aside; leaving the app brings them back in the state you left them. AnyLyric’s own pages always hide the overlay. Requires the accessibility service below.
No foreground switch has arrived yet. Switch to the app you want to hide in, then come back — its package name will show up here.
The accessibility service is not connected, so no foreground switch can arrive. Turn it on first, then come back.
Not enabled — tap to open system settings
Enabled but not connected — tap to reopen system settings
Also turn on the accessibility service below, or nothing will be hidden.

Two jobs: (1) tell AnyLyric which app is in the foreground so the overlay steps aside in the apps you choose; (2) read the text of music notifications (transport-category only) so lyrics still work on head units that block the notification-access page. It never reads screen content and never records your input.
Scroll keeps one line and moves it sideways; the frame height no longer changes with the lyric.
Drag the slider to resize; the overlay follows while you drag. Far left is Auto — the frame hugs the text. A fixed height stays fixed, so longer or shorter lyrics never change it.
Hide when there are no lyrics
Shift context lines to the right to form a staircase. Left alignment only.
Enter edit mode to drag the overlay where you want it; size is set with the sliders above
Long press the overlay to lock it, hide it for 10 minutes, open settings or copy the current line. Position and size are stored as ratios, so they survive resolution changes.
Drag to move · long press for more
Sample lyrics — set the size in Settings
Grant the overlay permission first, then adjust size and position.
Required. Lets AnyLyric read the media session of the player that is already playing.
Required. Used only to draw the lyric overlay.

This device rejected every settings shortcut.

Open it manually:
%1$s

Attempts:
%2$s
Settings → Notification access → find AnyLyric in the list (alphabetical, near the top) and turn the switch on
Settings → Apps → Special app access → Display over other apps → find AnyLyric and turn the switch on

The system page did not open (some head units answer with "multimedia not supported"), or the switch is still off.

Open it manually — try both paths:
① Settings → Apps → Special app access → Notification access → turn on AnyLyric
② Settings → Notifications (or "Notifications & status bar") → Notification access → turn on AnyLyric

Come back to this page afterwards; the status turns into "Connected".
If neither path lists this item, this head unit does not expose notification access to third-party apps — the lyrics cannot be read here, and this is not an installation problem.
One step left: display over other apps

The system page did not open, or the switch is still off.

Open it manually:
① Settings → Apps → Special app access → Display over other apps → turn on AnyLyric
② Some head units call it "floating window"; it is also under App info → AnyLyric → Permissions

Come back to this page afterwards; the status updates by itself.
Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps → AnyLyric → turn “AnyLyric foreground detection” on
Notification access granted — waiting for the system to connect…
Granted, but the system did not reconnect
Notification access not granted — lyrics unavailable
Connected through the car\'s direct channel — no permission needed
AnyLyric is running — waiting for playback
Off: nothing is captured and nothing is allocated. On: the probe records what each player exposes, plus this app\'s resource usage once a minute.
No app can receive the file. Use Copy instead.
Plays no audio, requests no audio focus, controls nothing, reads no files. Network is used only to check for updates.
nothing published in the release repo yet
Mirrors and CDN first, GitHub direct as the last fallback. Best for most networks.
Only the official address. Always the most up to date, but often times out in mainland China.
Global CDN. Right after a release the mirror may still serve the previous manifest.
Public GitHub proxy. It only forwards bytes; the package is still verified by SHA-256.
Public GitHub proxy, a spare node for gh-proxy.com.
Acceleration node. Availability varies with the network in use.
Mirror node. Usually slower, often reachable when other lines fail.
Tap any row to pick a color. Each one has its own default.
Total lyric lines. The current line wraps first; whatever budget is left goes to the following lines.
Draw a thin outline around the text. Almost required on a bright background.
Draw nothing when no lyrics are available. Off shows a small “No lyrics” note instead.
When every local channel misses, look the song up online by title and artist. This is the only path that lets the lyrics chain use the network. Off by default.
A small tab on the left edge. Tap it to collapse or expand the overlay.
“Song · Artist”, centered above or below the lyrics.
Both permissions are required. Grant them on this screen — no computer needed.
If this head unit has no notification-access entry at all, turn on the Accessibility switch below instead: AnyLyric will read the song name from music notifications and fetch the lyrics online.

This head unit does not expose notification access (the car maker blocks that page), so that switch can be left alone. The car\'s own media service hands over the song info and lyrics without any permission — status: %1$s.

The permission is already ticked; the system just has not bound the service yet. It usually recovers within seconds, and lyrics keep working meanwhile. If it never does, tap System settings and toggle the switch off and on.

Notification access is granted but the system has not bound the service. AnyLyric is polling media sessions at a low rate instead, and lyrics work normally; it switches back to push automatically once connected. No action needed.

Automatic reconnect did not take effect on this device. Tap System settings, open AnyLyric\'s notification access page and toggle it off and on — this is a system-level stall, not a missing permission.
Edit mode on: drag to move.
Edit mode off: touches pass through.
Nothing is collected while debug is off — no sampling, no bookkeeping, no extra calls. Turn it on in Settings → Debug to get live state, source attempts and resource usage here.
Live probe data is disabled.\n\nTurn on Settings → Debug, then come back to this page.
Notification access is not granted. Tick AnyLyric in system settings, then come back.
Notification access is ticked, but the system has not bound the service yet. Tap Reconnect; if that fails, toggle the switch off and on in system settings.
Overlay permission is missing. Grant the display-over-other-apps permission.
No app is publishing a media session. Start playback in the car player or a third-party player.
A media session exists but is not playing. Press play in that app.
The player updates the title only while paused. This is a publishing-side AVRCP limitation, not an AnyLyric bug.
This player exposes no lyric channel at all. Nothing is wrong with AnyLyric; another source would be needed.
The player reports a position that repeatedly jumps back a little. Timed lyrics may drift; the cause is on the publishing side.
The overlay was not attached. Check the overlay permission and try again.
The overlay is attached but has no size. Likely a layout problem.
“Hide when no lyrics” is on and there is nothing to show, so the overlay is hidden on purpose.
Hidden by app: the current foreground app is in your hide list, so the overlay steps aside. Expected behavior; it comes back when you leave that app.

“Hide in apps” is on, but the accessibility service is not connected, so none of the selected apps will hide the overlay. Some ROMs disable it after an app update — turn it on again in system settings.
A player is pinned under Player channel, but it has no media session right now. Set it back to Automatic, or start playback in that player.

Working through the car\'s direct channel. Notification access is not granted (this head unit blocks that page), but the car\'s media service hands over the song info and lyrics without any permission — lyrics are coming from %1$s.
Working as designed. Lyrics are being taken from %1$s.
